title: Define the requirements engineer role in Athena
summary: Add a read-only "requirements-engineer" role definition (name, goal, fixed prompt, cadence, rung limit) beside the steward, audience and auditor in roles.rs. Its prompt covers owning the spec and shared vocabulary, turning Sri's words into sourced requirements with open questions, and checking a job's spec against what Sri meant, leaving how to build it to a planner. Audience is Sri and the reviewers of the Olympus rollout.

defaults_applied.how: Role is a Rust definition in roles.rs.
Unit tests for the new role; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One role definition plus its doc, no wiring.
Tests check the role's validity and prompt content, not mere existence.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Doc comments and design doc written for outside readers.
Prose-only protection of the prompt is marked as such, as for the auditor.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Decision 4 is read as: define the role (a recorded definition like the auditor), not build the spec file (decision 3), vocabulary file (decision 5) or planner.
No CLI command or job-pipeline wiring is added now; like the auditor it could be run later on request.
The role reads and records only, with highest_rung Implementation, since spec changes need Sri's approval.
Role identity is named requirements-engineer, version 1.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: a new test shows requirements_engineer(at) validates, has path records/roles/requirements-engineer-1.json, and its prompt is under a stated length bound.

The role prompt states that it owns the spec and the shared vocabulary, that each requirement cites the words of Sri it came from, that open questions are recorded rather than guessed, and that it checks each job's spec against what Sri meant.

The prompt and docs say the role does not decide how to build (a planner does), and that spec changes are proposals Sri approves, not self-made changes. The rung limit is no higher than the existing rule allows (nobody changes the top two rungs).

docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md has a section on the requirements engineer citing BRIEF.md addendum 2026-10-17 items 3C, 4A and 5A as its source, so a reader can see what it is for and what it is not.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test`: all clean and passing.
No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, or records/ file changes; the spec file, vocabulary file and planner are not built here.

out_of_scope: Creating the cohesive spec or the vocabulary file
Wiring a CLI command or running the role in the job pipeline
Rewriting BRIEF.md or renaming to Olympus
departures: Slightly lower acceptance: the request is a decision, not a change, so scope (definition only) is an interpretation. Slightly higher pass odds: the change mirrors existing role patterns.
